title: Tests that allow any aftershock rate find no clear magnitude change in 192 first USGS forecast regions
abstract: We tested magnitude marks in 192 first USGS generic aftershock forecast regions. The method allows any event rate that depends on past magnitudes. It does not condition on the final event count. A beta predictive likelihood divided by the maximum constant-mark likelihood gives a safe test for changes in the high-magnitude share. A second test checks the issued b-value. In 335 recorded events on days 1-30, neither test type rejected after correction across 384 tests. Puerto Rico had 25 high marks in 84 early events and 18 in 73 late events. This does not show that catalog loss explains its earlier time-curve rejection. The strongest b-value evidence was 3613, below the joint threshold of 7680. The sample and the conservative tests have low power. We provide a proof, an exact path check, code, aggregate results, and a simulation that shows failure of an ordinary binomial test under selected stopping. This is a reanalysis of one revised catalog snapshot, not an independent replication or a new general statistical theorem.
